long_biography.plain_text:
Firoz Lalji endowed an African research centre at the London School of Economics through his family foundation. It developed into the Firoz Lalji Institute for Africa, bringing research, teaching and public discussion about the continent into the university's work. His educational giving also established postgraduate scholarships for students from Uganda and Belize and helped create a leadership programme for African graduate students.

Lalji came from a merchant family in Kampala whose businesses were seized during Uganda's expulsion of people of Asian descent. An economics graduate of the London School of Economics, he left the country with his family in 1972 and settled in Canada.

confidence.reason: Actual university descriptions establish educational gifts and programme beneficiaries; the business-organisation profile and LSE corroborate formative Uganda-to-Canada history.
